chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, all from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Abu Jameela, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to teach me a supplication for sustenance, so he taught me a supplication which I had not seen more abundant for sustenance than it. He said: Say:

O Allah, grant me from Your extensive Grace a permissible, goodly sustenance, an extensive, permissible, goodly sustenance that suffices for the world and the Hereafter, poured out, welcome, wholesome, without toil and without favor from any of Your creatures, except as an extension from Your extensive Grace, for You said: 'And ask Allah of His Grace'.
So from Your Grace I ask, and from Your Gift I ask, and from Your Full Hand I ask.
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia supplication for abundant and permissible sustenance?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this supplication highlights the Shia emphasis on seeking halal provision that ensures spiritual and material sufficiency without the burden of hardship or dependence on creation. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the act of asking directly to the Quranic imperative, reinforcing the theological principle that sustenance is a divine gift accessed through humble petition.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, and Al Husayn Bin Saeed, altogether from Al Qasim Bin Urwa, from Abu Jameela, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> to teach me a supplication for the sustenance, so he<sup>asws</sup> taught me a supplication what I had not seen as more beneficial than it for the sustenance. Said say:

Heasws said: ‘Say, ‘O Allahazwj! Sustain me from Yourazwj Grace, the extensive, the Permissible, the goodly sustenance, extensive, Permissible, goodly, adequate for the world and the Hereafter, attained, achieved, welcoming, wholesome, from without a toil nor from anyone from Yourazwj creatures except as being an extension from Yourazwj Expansive Grace, for Youazwj Said [4:32] and ask Allah of His Grace.
Thus, it is from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Grace that I ask, and from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Gifts I ask, and from Your<sup>azwj</sup> Full Hands I ask’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Sa’Id all from al-Qasim ibn ‘Urwah from abu Jamilah from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘ Ammar who has said the following:
“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) to instruct me with a supplication for sustenance and he taught me one. 1 had not found anything else as attracting sustenance as this. The Imam said, ‘Say

O Lord, grant me out of Your vast magnanimity, lawful and pure sustenance, that is vast, lawful, pure and sufficient for this world and the hereafter in large quantities, pleasant in nutrition with out toiling or being obliged by any of Your creatures except for its being the extra from Your vast generosity; You have said, “. . . ask Allah from His munificence. . . .” (4: 32)
, from Your munificence I ask sustenance and from Your charity I beg and from Your wealthy hand I plead to receive help.’”
